## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

This **replaces** the earlier tolerance listed in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` under
"Code Conventions" ("Comments: French or English both accepted"): existing
French comments are not to be rewritten wholesale, but any new comment and
any edit to an existing comment must be in English.

```
// ✅ CORRECT
// retry with backoff because the API rate-limits bursts above 10 req/s

// ❌ WRONG (a French comment, which Rule 307 forbids)
// on relance avec un backoff car l'API limite les rafales au-delà de 10 req/s
```

```
✅ fix: correct table width calculation when a column is dropped

Bordures étaient soustraites deux fois, ce qui tronquait la dernière colonne.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

❌ fix: corrige le calcul de largeur de colonne
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ A commit message written in French, even partially
- ❌ A new code comment in French
- ❌ Confusing this rule with the language of the conversation, which
  remains the user's

</system-reminder>

**A kind is not reserved for batches.** `create` and `delete` in the explorer
are single-item runs against a forge, and they are registered for the three
things the registry gives that a local flag does not: the blink phase comes
from `jobs.FrameMsg` rather than from a view's own chain — the explorer's stops on
`!m.loading`, so a phase taken from it would freeze the moment the tree settled;
the `busy()` guard sees work started anywhere; and `Run.Context` is stamped at
launch, so a create that outlives a context switch cannot write into the tree it
switched to. What decides is whether the work is a network call the user has to

---
| Session | the first 8 characters of the ID. `Optional`: the first column dropped on a narrow terminal. The filter (`/`) matches the full ID. |

- **Rule 139.** The body is always `m.table.View()`. Loading, an empty
  machine and a filter with no match all leave a table with its header.
- **Header** (`GetHeaderInfo`): `Sessions` (rows visible after the filter) and,
  only when non-zero, `Skipped` (`Listing.Omitted`).
- **Footer** (Rule 128), derived on every frame with no timer, in this order:
  a failed read (red, "Failed to list Claude Code sessions — check logs"; the
  error is logged, never shown, since it can name a path), then loading (spinner,
  "Reading Claude Code sessions..."), then "No Claude Code sessions found in
  <root>" when the listing is empty before any filter.
- **Shortcuts**: `ctrl+r` Refresh, `/` Filter, `?` Help. The same keys in every
  state, none greyed (Rule 130): each always acts. `.` cycles the sort column
  and is listed in `?` only (Rule 138).
- **Reload on every entry.** The view is built once and stays cached in the
  router (`createView` stops if it already exists). The reload comes from
  `switchView` (`internal/app/command_line.go`), which calls `Init()` on every
  entry, and `Init` starts a read. The rows from the previous visit stay on
  screen until the answer arrives. Unlike `ctrl+r`, this entry reload shows no
  spinner and no "Reading..." line, because `Init` cannot set `loading` to
  true. `ctrl+r` reads again under a new generation number, and a stale answer
  (older generation) is dropped. A failed refresh keeps the previous rows: they
  are dated, not wrong.
- **Rule 110.** `listSessionsCmd` resolves `ProjectsRoot()` and calls
  `ListSessions` inside the `Cmd` and returns a message; `Update` alone touches
  the model.

- **Header** (before DEVDESK-47): `Agents`, `Tokens` (sum of Total), both following the filter, and
  `Updates` (`live` or `paused`, see "Live updates"); the list above adds the cost fields.
- **Footer status**: a failed read (red, "Failed to read this session — check
  logs"), then loading (a full read only; spinner, "Reading session..."), then, when
  `Diagnostics.Degraded()`, a warning "Totals are approximate — some transcript
  data could not be read", then a price hint (Info, a state derived on every frame):
  with no price configured and tokens in the session, "Set agent_usage.prices in this
  context's config file to estimate costs — see ?"; with prices but a model without
`ParseSession`: the model holds one `*Aggregate` per open session, and each
read applies a `Delta` to it.

**The polling chain.** Opening a session starts a full read (cursor
`Rewound()`, spinner, "Reading session..."). Each answer schedules the next
step: wait `pollInterval` (2 s, `pollTickCmd`), then `startRead(false)` reads
from the cursor, silently (no spinner). At most one read and one tick exist per
`agentGen`: `reading` blocks a tick that arrives while a read is in flight, and
a tick or an answer of another generation is dropped. An empty delta changes
nothing on screen; a non-empty or full one rebuilds the rows (`withUsage`).
is back. With `app.when_unfocused: run` the router sends `Focused:true`, so none
of this happens.

**`ctrl+r` is a full read.** It rewinds the cursor (`Cursor.Rewound()`), reads
everything again, and shows the spinner. If a read is already in flight, it is
never doubled (one per `Aggregate`): `fullPending` is set and the full read
starts when that read answers, whether it succeeded or failed.

**Leaving and coming back** (`LeavingView`, see `app-shell.md`).
- `Leave()` bumps `agentGen`, which drops any tick or read in flight, and
  clears `reading` and `agentsLoading`. The open session and its rows stay. If
  a full read was in flight (a `ctrl+r`, or the open's first read), `Leave` sets
  `fullPending`, so the resume repeats it. It always returns `true`.
- `switchView` calls `Init()` on every entry; at the agents level `Init` adds
  `resumeCmd()`, which answers `agentsResumeMsg`. `handleResume` bumps
  `agentGen` again, clears `pollStopped` and starts a read from the cursor,
  silent: coming back reads what changed while away, and goes back to live if
  the session is still being written. With `fullPending`, the read is full and
  has its spinner.

**The cursor stays on the same agent.** `selection.go` gives each agent a
stable key: `main` for the orchestrator, `sub:<ID>#n` for a sub-agent, `n`

- **Footer status**: a failed read (red, "Failed to read this session — check
  logs"), then loading (a full read only; spinner, "Reading session..."), then, when
  `Diagnostics.Degraded()`, a warning "Totals are approximate — some transcript
  data could not be read", then a price hint (Info, a state derived on every frame):
  with no price configured and tokens in the session, "Set agent_usage.prices in this
  context's config file to estimate costs — see ?"; with prices but a model without
`ParseSession`: the model holds one `*Aggregate` per open session, and each
read applies a `Delta` to it.

**The polling chain.** Opening a session starts a full read (cursor
`Rewound()`, spinner, "Reading session..."). Each answer schedules the next
step: wait `pollInterval` (2 s, `pollTickCmd`), then `startRead(false)` reads
from the cursor, silently (no spinner). At most one read and one tick exist per
`agentGen`: `reading` blocks a tick that arrives while a read is in flight, and
a tick or an answer of another generation is dropped. An empty delta changes
nothing on screen; a non-empty or full one rebuilds the rows (`withUsage`).
is back. With `app.when_unfocused: run` the router sends `Focused:true`, so none
of this happens.

**`ctrl+r` is a full read.** It rewinds the cursor (`Cursor.Rewound()`), reads
everything again, and shows the spinner. If a read is already in flight, it is
never doubled (one per `Aggregate`): `fullPending` is set and the full read
starts when that read answers, whether it succeeded or failed.

**Leaving and coming back** (`LeavingView`, see `app-shell.md`).
- `Leave()` bumps `agentGen`, which drops any tick or read in flight, and
  clears `reading` and `agentsLoading`. The open session and its rows stay. If
  a full read was in flight (a `ctrl+r`, or the open's first read), `Leave` sets
  `fullPending`, so the resume repeats it. It always returns `true`.
- `switchView` calls `Init()` on every entry; at the agents level `Init` adds
  `resumeCmd()`, which answers `agentsResumeMsg`. `handleResume` bumps
  `agentGen` again, clears `pollStopped` and starts a read from the cursor,
  silent: coming back reads what changed while away, and goes back to live if
  the session is still being written. With `fullPending`, the read is full and
  has its spinner.

**The cursor stays on the same agent.** `selection.go` gives each agent a
stable key: `main` for the orchestrator, `sub:<ID>#n` for a sub-agent, `n`

content.content:
completion leaves a row spinning for the life of the view.
- **"Nothing scanned yet" waits for the caches to answer** (`inventoryLoading`,
  D65). An empty table covers two opposite facts — both caches replied and there
  is nothing, or `loadInventoryCmd` is still in flight — and branching on
  `len(Items()) == 0` alone asserts the first about the second. The table stays
  on screen while it loads and the footer carries the spinner (Rule 139).

**What the row says.** `setInventory` stamps each `scanTarget` with
`Activity` (`components.DescribeRow`, through `rowActivity`) and `ScanRunning`
logs`; for an image, the raw reference, not the alias); the row detail returns
afterwards. A failure posed from `ws` or OCI posts no event here. At 60 columns
`Scanned` is dropped (it is `Optional`), so `scanning` is not visible there; the
dot and the footer carry the state.

**The view's own spinner is for loads only.** `spinnerAlive()` —
`inventoryLoading || remediationBusy()` — decides whether the view's own
`spinner.Model` chain keeps going (`handleSpinnerTick` renews it,
`spinnerTickIfIdle` refuses a second chain alongside a live one). It no longer
answers for scans: those are the router's animation. The footer's two marks
have separate writers (DEVDESK-341): the view's own chain feeds the braille
spinner frame (`SetSpinnerFrame`) for loads, the router's `FrameMsg` feeds the
activity dot's phase (`SetBlinkPhase`, in `handleFrameMsg`) for scans. The dot
shows only when no inventory load is in progress. For the same reason as
before, `reloadInventory` takes its tick *before* raising the flag.

`esc` and `ctrl+r` return to the inventory, or to the list the results were
opened from when `OriginView` is set.


## Scan Cache

Two independent disk+memory caches in `internal/cache/`:
`:sec` gained the most. `scanTarget.Scanning` was a flag the view set and
cleared, and `handleInventoryLoaded` carried it across every reload by hand: the
caches say nothing about a scan that has not finished writing to them, so a
refresh landing mid-rescan cleared the spinner and left the row looking settled.
That reconciliation is *gone* rather than fixed: the row's activity is derived
in `setInventory` (see "The security inventory"), so a reload has nothing to
preserve. With DEVDESK-145 the failure is derived too, from the registry's
failure memory, and `scanTarget.Failed` is removed.

**A load is not a job.** The view keeps its own `spinner.Model` for reading the
caches, fetching the image list and the Remediation tab; scans are the router's
animation (D5) and no longer touch it.

**`rescanCmd` had no starting message** — only a finished one — so a target went
from queued straight to done and nothing said which of a batch was actually
running. `InventoryScanStartingMsg` exists for that (D10), and like the others
it is emitted *after* the worker pool hands out a slot, which is what makes
`queued` and `running` mean different things.


## A scan can be stopped — `K` in `:jobs` (D7)

**The scan form is gone** (phase 3), and with it `StateScanning`: there is no
screen that runs one scan and waits on it. The inventory rescans in the
background with a spinner on the row, the way the images list does. What went
with the form, because nothing else read it:

| Gone | Why it existed |
under a lock, since scans of several candidates finish together.

The scans are not in the jobs registry (`:jobs`): the tab keeps its own set of
images in flight and its own spinner, like the inventory's load. Trivy runs one
process at a time (`scan.trivySem`), so the scans queue there rather than in
parallel, and `max_concurrent_scans` does not apply to them.

opened from when `OriginView` is set.


## Scan Cache

Two independent disk+memory caches in `internal/cache/`:
`:sec` gained the most. `scanTarget.Scanning` was a flag the view set and
cleared, and `handleInventoryLoaded` carried it across every reload by hand: the
caches say nothing about a scan that has not finished writing to them, so a
refresh landing mid-rescan cleared the spinner and left the row looking settled.
That reconciliation is *gone* rather than fixed: the row's activity is derived
in `setInventory` (see "The security inventory"), so a reload has nothing to
preserve. With DEVDESK-145 the failure is derived too, from the registry's
failure memory, and `scanTarget.Failed` is removed.

**A load is not a job.** The view keeps its own `spinner.Model` for reading the
caches, fetching the image list and the Remediation tab; scans are the router's
animation (D5) and no longer touch it.

**`rescanCmd` had no starting message** — only a finished one — so a target went
from queued straight to done and nothing said which of a batch was actually
running. `InventoryScanStartingMsg` exists for that (D10), and like the others
it is emitted *after* the worker pool hands out a slot, which is what makes
`queued` and `running` mean different things.


## A scan can be stopped — `K` in `:jobs` (D7)

**The scan form is gone** (phase 3), and with it `StateScanning`: there is no
screen that runs one scan and waits on it. The inventory rescans in the
background with a spinner on the row, the way the images list does. What went
with the form, because nothing else read it:

| Gone | Why it existed |
under a lock, since scans of several candidates finish together.

The scans are not in the jobs registry (`:jobs`): the tab keeps its own set of
images in flight and its own spinner, like the inventory's load. Trivy runs one
process at a time (`scan.trivySem`), so the scans queue there rather than in
parallel, and `max_concurrent_scans` does not apply to them.

`theme.StringWidth(glyph) - lipgloss.Width(glyph)` (the East Asian ambiguous
width correction, as for a detail line) so the line is `width` columns for
`runewidth` too.

The spinner frame is the **rendered** `spinner.View()`, not a bare frame: every
view already styles its spinner with `theme.SpinnerStyle()`, and restyling would
nest one escape inside another. It is measured with `lipgloss.Width`, which
ignores escapes — the opposite of a table cell's rule (Rule 122), and the
`RenderFooter`/`renderInfoLine`/`renderInfoText`, and
`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody` fails on a `theme.SpinnerMessage` in a
table view. The one screen that legitimately fills itself with a spinner — the
registry browser mid-pull, which has no table behind it — is written down as a
declared exception, the way `keymap.DeclaredExceptions()` is.

## Tables — `internal/ui/datatable`

The shared mechanism behind the application's tables: column widths, sorting,
| forge sign-in (`internal/ui/forge/auth`) | `model.go`, `update.go`, `view.go` | token required (trimmed) |

**Auth spinner fix.** In the sign-in view `handleEnterKey` set `authenticating`
and started the spinner, then `authenticate()` returned nil with "Token is
required" (or the missing-URL message) in the body: nothing ever cleared the
flag, so the spinner kept running. Validation now runs before `authenticating`
is set, for the token and for the missing URL, and a refused submit starts
nothing. A stored token made only of blanks no longer triggers the auto-login
(`handleCredentialsLoaded`) either.

**Out of scope.** `internal/ui/templates/form.go`, netdiag, the `ctrl+p` palette
and `FilterBar` do not use the underline yet.

193	the pending text, with no blink. Without a `SetBlinkPhase`
194	call the dot is steady on. `●` and `○` are one column wide and share a width,
